children: Arabica coffee futures hit a 2-1/2-month low on Thursday, with exchange stocks edging away from a recent 27-year low, while sugar and cocoa prices also fell sharply.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 5.05 cents, or 1.8%, at $2.765 per lb, after hitting a 2-1/2-month low of $2.7460.
* Dealers noted increases in ICE arabica stocks, although they remain far below year-earlier levels.

* Exchange stocks rose for the second consecutive day on Thursday to 247,887 bags, up from a 27-year low of 217,646 bags earlier this week. All the fresh coffee (14,532 bags) came from Brazil. The grading team rejected 5,715 bags.
* At the same time last year, stocks stood at 668,874 bags.

* Dave Behrends, head of trading at Sucafina, said several confirmed bearish factors happened all at once to drive the market lower, such as increased Brazil exports, beneficial weather in Brazil and Vietnam and rising ICE stocks.
* Robusta coffee
fell 1.1% to $3,391 a metric ton.
* Recent rains in top robusta producer Vietnam have the potential to be beneficial for coffee trees, a trader based in the country's coffee belt said.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
​settled down 0.55 cent, or 3.1%, at 17.42 cents per lb, after setting a three-week low of 17.37 cents.
* Dealers said a downward correction for sugar was expected after recent strong gains, also under the impact of the FED rate increase.

* Peak Research said in a note that agricultural commodities have gone down historically in the weeks and months after the start of a new cycle of U.S. rate increases, as part of the money from investors move to fixed-income.
* One broker also noted a period of dry weather in Brazil, at last, that will allow mills to boost cane processing.
* White sugar
fell 2.9% to $508.60 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled down £125, or 2.9%, to £4,252  per ton.
* New York cocoa
fell 3.5% to $5,772 a ton, having hit a five-week low of $5,506 earlier.
* Dealers said supplies remained ample with London December trading at a discount of around £173 to March (LCC-1=R).
